label: D-Link DGS-1210-28P
description: D-Link DGS-1210-28P (Rev F) smart managed PoE switch: 24x 10/100/1000BASE-T PoE+ RJ-45 on a 193 W budget, 4x 1G RJ45/SFP combo ports, 56 Gbps, 41.7 Mpps, two fans.

fabric.note: 56 Gbps switching capacity and 41.7 Mpps maximum 64-byte forwarding rate for the DGS-1210-28P, from the DGS-1210 Series Rev F datasheet specification table (https://www.dlink.com/us/en/-/media/business_products/dgs/dgs-1210/datasheet/dgs1210seriesrevfdatasheet211enus.pdf). 28 ports x 2 Gbps full duplex, so an RJ45/SFP combo pair counts once whichever medium is in use.

notes: Ports, per the DGS-1210 Series Rev F datasheet (hardware Rev. F, 2.11 EN US, 05-SEP-2018): 24 x 10/100/1000BASE-T PoE (802.3af/at) on ports 1-24 plus 4 x 10/100/1000 or 100/1000 SFP combo ports (one port, two cages, one medium at a time). 8K MAC entries, 256 static MAC entries, 4.1 Mbits packet buffer, DDR3 128 MB CPU memory, 32 MB flash, 256 static VLAN groups (VID 1-4094), 802.1D/802.1w/802.1s STP, 802.3ad LACP (8 groups of up to 8 ports), jumbo frames to 10,000 bytes, and 124 IPv4 / 50 IPv6 static routes over 4 IP interfaces - static routing, not a routing protocol, which is what puts this in the L3-lite class. Management is web GUI, compact CLI over Telnet, SNMP v1/v2c/v3 and D-Link Network Assistant; no model in the line has a serial console port (the console row in the datasheet is an LED, not a port). Dual software images and dual configuration files. 2 fans, 440 x 250 x 44 mm, 3.75 kg, 263.9 W at 100 V with PoE enabled, 30.6 W with PoE disabled. Two fans at 51.7 dB(A) high / 44.9 dB(A) low. A combo port is one port with two cages and only one medium active at a time, which is why 56 Gbps = 28 ports x 2 Gbps rather than 32. Source: https://www.dlink.com/us/en/-/media/business_products/dgs/dgs-1210/datasheet/dgs1210seriesrevfdatasheet211enus.pdf

poe.note: 193 W PoE budget for ports 1-24, from the Rev F specification table and ordering information; the four combo RJ45 ports 25-28 are not PoE capable. 24 x 15.4 W = 369.6 W of 802.3af exceeds the budget too, so at full 802.3af load the budget is the limit: 193 W covers about 12 ports at 15.4 W or 6 at 30 W.
